items.stem: A company reports a healthy profit yet cannot pay suppliers. The most likely explanation is:

options.text: Cash is tied up in receivables and inventory, so profit is not yet cash
options.rationale: Correct: accrual profit differs from cash due to working-capital timing.

options.text: Profit and cash are always identical, so the report is wrong

options.rationale: Depreciation is a non-cash expense; it does not add cash.

items.explanation: Correct: accrual profit differs from cash due to working-capital timing.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the primary financial statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The balance sheet is a snapshot at a point in time
options.rationale: Correct: it reports position on a date.

options.text: The cash flow statement shows movements of cash over a period
options.rationale: Correct: it explains the change in cash.

options.text: The income statement reports the closing bank balance
options.rationale: That is not what the income statement shows.

options.text: The balance sheet reports revenue for the year
options.rationale: Revenue is on the income statement.

items.explanation: Correct: it reports position on a date.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A manager must choose between two projects returning the same total cash but at different times. All else equal, finance theory prefers the one that:

options.text: Returns cash sooner, because earlier cash is worth more
options.rationale: Correct: the time value of money favours earlier cash.

options.text: Returns cash later, to defer effort
options.rationale: Later cash is worth less in present-value terms.

options.text: Has the larger number of line items
Is championed by the most senior manager

items.explanation: Correct: the time value of money favours earlier cash.
